analysis.title: Markets catch their breath: equities rebound, dollar retreats
key_insights: Tech stocks rebounded on Monday after last week's decline. The Philadelphia semiconductor index gained 5.5% (SOX +6.3% by the European close after +4.2% last Friday), even as Nvidia fell on reports of an investigation tied to allegations concerning its CEO, Jensen Huang.

Brent declined further towards $91.10/barrel on unconfirmed reports of Iranian concessions regarding the Strait of Hormuz. EUR rates initially fell with oil, but the move faded as Brent rebounded from its lows.
The US Treasury curve flattened ahead of major auctions: $58bn 3-year notes on Monday, $42bn 10-year notes on Tuesday and $25bn long-term bonds on Thursday.
The dollar retreated against most G10 currencies. DXY fell to about 101.6-101.9 and EUR/USD rose to about 1.12. NZD/USD and AUD/USD were the top G10 performers on improved risk appetite.

US October CPI is due today at 14:30. Natixis says it could confirm or call into question the dollar's recent retreat via Fed repricing. Goolsbee warned that data-centre investment could reignite services inflation.

Peripheral and semi-core European debt benefited most from the risk-on move. The 10-year OAT-Bund spread fell below 150 bps for the first time since mid-October, and the 10-year Bund yield closed near 3.25%.

European equities rebounded: SXXE +1.8%, banks and tech up more than 3% on average, luxury down less than 1%. V2X fell 2 points to 19.3. In the US, NDX gained 3% and SPX nearly 2% by the European close despite Nvidia falling 6% at the open.

Credit tightened: iTraxx Main -2.7 bps, Crossover -12 bps, CDX IG -2 bps. US tech credit also tightened: SpaceX -6 bps, Oracle -5 bps, Broadcom -4 bps. Booking issued €3.5bn across four tranches with new-issue premiums of 17-21 bps.

UniCredit (UCGIM) posted a Q3-26 beat with record profit. Revenues rose 12% to €6.9bn, operating expenses fell 1% to €2.3bn and net income rose 24% to €3.3bn. Full-year net profit guidance was raised to 'well above' €11.5bn, and cost of risk was the only miss. Regulatory clearance for the Commerzbank (CMZB) deal is expected late this month, with control in early 2027.

SoftBank Group reported a ¥1.12tn net loss for the quarter on a $3.73bn data-center charge and lower Vision Fund gains, despite higher-than-expected sales. China blocked its planned acquisition of ABB's robotics unit. SoftBank Corp. raised full-year forecasts but is reassessing US neocloud plans over datacenter demand concerns.

market_movers.rationale: Nvidia fell about 6% at the open on reports of an investigation linked to allegations concerning its CEO, though the Nasdaq 100 still gained 3% on dip buying.

earnings_insights: UniCredit Q3-26 (reported): revenues +12% y/y to €6.9bn, net income +24% to €3.3bn, operating expenses -1% to €2.3bn, CET1 ratio 15.0% at end-Q3-26. Cost of risk was the only miss. Full-year net profit guidance raised to 'well above' €11.5bn.
SoftBank Group Q2-27 (partial, reported): net loss of ¥1.12tn on sales above expectations, with a $3.73bn data-center charge and net finance costs up 164% y/y.
SoftBank Corp. H1-27 (reported): revenues +11.7%, with full-year revenue, operating profit and net income forecasts raised.
Upcoming this week: CoreWeave, Cisco and Applied Materials report earnings.
